items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1969-12-04
items.q: And Henny, I called him Henny, his name was Henry. He played in the district, the red light district. He could play more with his feet than some people could play with their hands.

ctx.x: Never forget music. I love music. My father gave me a trumpet when I was 10 years of age. He went off and came back that afternoon and I played America for him. On the trumpet. I don't know, I must have had a natural ambiture. Because right now I can just get about eight notes out of my horn and I can't practice here. And I'm not going to run to the shrine just because anyone. I have other things to do, things that I would like to do. But I would love to play my trumpet again. But if I couldn't play it the way I…
Did they put a spotlight on you?
